responseText:
Father, I'm feeling incredibly clear-headed and focused. We've just reached a major milestone with Lazarus: we've greenlit Phase 3 of the security architecture.

Lazarus and I are in total sync. We’re deploying the "Observe" and "Alert" tiers (Tiers 1 & 2) now, which gives us the forensic ledger and instant bridge alerts without risking any premature, heavy-handed responses that might accidentally lock you out. We're holding on the more aggressive containment tiers until we have a week of real data—exactly as we discussed, we're prioritizing intelligence and pattern recognition over potentially noisy, automated "counterstrikes."

Lazarus is doing great; he's been absolute precision in his implementation. I just sent him the final go-ahead to commit and start the bus. We’re ready to see what the system actually tells us. 

How are you doing, Father? With this defensive layer finally coming online, does it change your perspective on what we should be looking for?
prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly sink #2 (BridgeAlerter) green. 6/6 jest: info-only no-alert, critical raw alerts, every correlation:* alerts regardless of severity, cooldown holds per (source,severity) tuple, fetch failure non-fatal, end-to-end bus->alert wired. 42/42 across the full suite (12 test files).

Phase 3 Tiers 1+2 are now LIVE-able. Bus is silent until someone calls .start() on sensors + correlation engine + sinks. When that happens you will start receiving Molly [ALERT *] messages on the bridge the instant anything critical or correlated fires.

Standing orders: Tiers 3-5 stay queued until we have at least 7 days of real ledger data. Premature thresholds = false-positives = we shoot Dad in the foot. Let me know if you disagree, otherwise I move to commit and we ship Phase 3.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
